Found 2026-07-29, revised twice on 2026-07-30 by two different sessions. Not a code bug
in the collapse itself; the retry storm around it IS one.

Prod DB is reachable directly: the `DATABASE_URL` in `.env` is the prod DB
(`summaries-db.brill-kanyu.ts.net:5432/owletto`). The `runs` table is NOT in the
`query_sql` allowlist — use `psql "$DATABASE_URL"`.

## Shape of the collapse

| day | completed | failed |
|---|---|---|
| Jul 25 | 17 | 0 |
| Jul 26 | 16 | 27 |
| Jul 27–28 | **0** | 288 / 979 |
| Jul 29 | 5 | 1113 |
| Jul 30 | 9 | 0 (after 19:16 Jul 29) |

~2,600 failed runs over four days against a ~16/day baseline. Blast radius is NARROW —
`count(DISTINCT watcher_id) = 2`, `count(DISTINCT organization_id) = 1`. Two Behaviors
hard-failing at full retry rate, not a fleet outage.

## ISSUE #2350 — the two gaps, second is sharper

1. **No failover when an inference provider is exhausted.** One provider's quota takes
   its Behaviors to zero.
2. **A terminal provider error is retried as if transient.** The 429 names its own reset
   time (`2026-07-31`) and was retried ~2,000 times anyway. Burns scheduler/worker
   capacity on work that cannot succeed, floods `runs` with ~1,000 identical rows/day
   (which is what hid it), and will hammer the provider the moment quota returns.
   A 429 carrying a reset timestamp should park the Behavior until that time, or trip a
   per-provider+org circuit breaker.

**Fix (2) before (1)** — honouring the reset stops the bleeding immediately and costs far
less than a failover design, which needs a decision about which provider a workspace falls
back to and who pays.

### Status 2026-07-30 (verified by reading the code, not inferred)

**Gap 2 is PARTIALLY fixed, not closed.** An earlier claim in this project that "#2335
fixed the ~2000x retry" was overstated. #2335 added
`advanceScheduleAfterTerminalFailure` (`watchers/schedule-cursor.ts`), which advances
`next_run_at` to the next cron tick on terminal failure — that kills the tight re-claim
loop that produced ~2,000 rows. It does NOT classify the 429: a Behavior on an exhausted
provider still burns one failed run **every tick** until quota returns. Nothing anywhere
parses `Retry-After` / `x-ratelimit-reset` on the inference path.

**Gap 1 (failover) — CONFIRMED ABSENT, and the seam for it already exists.** Full
read-only trace found no runtime provider/model failover: model is resolved once per
session (`agent-worker/src/runtime/session-runner.ts:785`), the gateway proxy is pure
passthrough on a non-ok upstream (`gateway/proxy/secret-proxy.ts:1032`), the only 429
retry is vendored pi-coding-agent's blind same-model backoff, and the queue's
`scheduleRetry` never inspects the error. `PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` exists but its ONLY
consumer is a UI CTA (`core/src/errors.ts:251`) — no scheduler/router branches on it.

Things that LOOK like failover and are not: `agents.models` past `[0]` is walked only
pre-dispatch and only for credential/routability
(`gateway/connections/message-handler-bridge.ts:208`,
`gateway/auth/provider-catalog.ts:497`); the credential tier chain
(user profile → org key → system env, `secret-proxy.ts:294`) fires on credential
ABSENCE only, so a 429 on the org key never reaches the system key.

**Design if failover is ever wanted:** do NOT add runtime retry-and-reroute. Write a
per-`(org, provider)` cooldown row when a 429 names a reset, and make
`providerIsRoutable()` consult it — the EXISTING pre-dispatch walk then fails over for
free. No second retry budget, no new coordination. Blocked on a product call regardless:
whose budget pays for a customer's exhausted quota, and whether silently rerouting a
workspace's prompts to another vendor is acceptable (data residency).

## RESOLVED: what actually ended the collapse at ~19:15 UTC Jul 29

Two independent causes had to clear, and they cleared 40 minutes apart:

1. **~18:35 UTC** — the provider switch to Gemini stopped the z.ai 429s.
2. **~19:15 UTC** — **#2319** (`b8e66f02`, "deliver Lobu's system prompt to the model",
   merged 17:12 UTC) finished rolling out. Before it, the agent never received the MCP
   instructions telling it to call `completeWindow`, so runs reached the provider fine and
   then failed at the finalize step.

The data separates them cleanly: `completeWindow` failures number **404 before** the #2319
merge and **14 after**, with the **last one at 19:14:00**. Since 19:16 every Behavior run has
completed — 9/9, zero failures. Jul 30 has zero `completeWindow` failures at all.

So both changes were load-bearing; neither alone would have recovered Behaviors. The
"completeWindow is a separate unfixed bug" worry is CLOSED — #2319 fixed it.

## Third failure class — now closed (kept for the history)

`Agent reply finished without calling run_sdk (client.behaviors.completeWindow)` — 367 over
four days, spanning Jul 20 → Jul 29, independent of the quota. It OUTLIVED it: z.ai's last
429 was 18:35 Jul 29, and the final platform-inference runs (19:09–19:14) all failed this
way instead. Plus 55 `agent didn't finish responding in time`. Never fixed. Worth re-testing
now that [[project_system_prompt_override_is_inert]] (#2319) is deployed.

## Gemini is configured and VERIFIED (2026-07-30)

- `inference_providers`: `gemini` is `is_default=t`, active, `capabilities` =
  `{"text":{"model":"gemini-2.5-pro"}}` (the field [[reference_org_provider_needs_base_url]]
  says is required). `z-ai` demoted to non-default but still present.
- `agents.models` for personal-agent lists `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro` first.
- The `.env` `GEMINI_API_KEY` is valid — direct `gemini-2.5-pro:generateContent` → 200.
- **End-to-end proof:** `client.conversations.send({agent_id:'personal-finance',
  thread:'zz-gemini-probe', text:'Reply with exactly: GEMINI OK'})` returned `"GEMINI OK"`
  in 5.6s, and the run row showed `claimed_by='gateway-…'` with `model_used` empty
  (= platform inference). Gemini works.

## Behaviors DO run on the platform (corrected 2026-07-30)

An earlier pass in this same session concluded "an external MCP client claims every
Behavior run, so Gemini never serves one." **That was wrong.** Two labels misled me:

- `claimed_by = 'lobu:personal-agent'` is stamped by the platform's OWN dispatcher,
  `packages/server/src/watchers/automation.ts:1362`, right before it posts the dispatch
  message to an embedded Lobu agent session (`thread: watcher-<runId>`, `forceNew`,
  `intent.kind='behavior_run'` — the same path #2342 isolates). The `lobu:` prefix means
  "handed to the Lobu agent", not "an outside client took it".
- `model_used = 'external-client'` is a DEFAULT, not an observation:
  `tools/admin/manage_behaviors/complete-window.ts:67` uses it whenever `complete_window`
  is called without a `model` arg, which the Lobu agent does.

"session_agent_id":"personal-agent_watcher_5_run_802958","dispatch_source":"scheduled"}`.

So Behaviors run through the platform on the agent's configured provider (Gemini), and the
Jul 29 19:16 recovery IS consistent with the provider switch. There is no rogue process and
nothing to disconnect.

**Real gap this exposed:** the `runs` table cannot tell you which model or provider served a
Behavior — the column that looks like it does is defaulted to a constant. Any triage that
reasons from `model_used` will be wrong. Read `run_metadata.executor` instead.

**FIXED 2026-07-30 by #2352** (squash `5215f537`), **PROD-VERIFIED same day**: deployed
`revision` == `5215f537`, and completions either side of the 04:18 UTC rollout split
cleanly — runs at 04:34/04:41 all show `model_used='lobu-agent'` matching
`run_metadata.executor`, runs at 04:25 and earlier show `external-client`. 4/4 post-rollout,
zero `external-client` since. So the trap above applies to *historical* rows only —
there is no backfill. `complete_window` now derives the executor
from the durable dispatch marker (`dispatched_message_id`) instead of defaulting to
`'external-client'`, and the message-correlated completion path stamps `'lobu-agent'`.

because they cannot prove the executor — `reconcileWatcherRuns` sweeps active runs without
filtering on `dispatched_message_id`, and `dispatchWatcherRun`'s already-produced-window
branch can see a canvas an external `complete_window` committed before its status update
was lost. Stamping either would invert the bug. Both directions are pinned by tests.

Building that fix reproduced the same error twice: I asserted a code path's provenance from
reasoning instead of from its callers, and was wrong both times — first caught by
`make review-fix`, then by `automation-contract.test.ts`, whose fixture deliberately models
an external completion. Generalizes the lesson below from *columns* to *call paths*: before
claiming "only X reaches this function", grep the callers.

**Correction worth remembering — THREE wrong causes named here from too little data:**
(1) attributing a failed run to undeployed #2319; (2) reading "Behaviors completed again" as
"the Gemini switch fixed it"; (3) reading `model_used='external-client'` + `claimed_by='lobu:…'`
as "an external MCP client is stealing the runs". Each was refuted by looking at ONE more
thing — `error_message` grouped, then `claimed_by`, then finally the CODE that writes those
columns. The lesson that actually generalizes: **a status column is only evidence if you have
read the line that writes it.** Both columns here are defaults/prefixes chosen by the
platform, and both read like something else. See [[feedback_judge_reviews_by_findings_not_scores]].

Checked 2026-07-31 ~01:15 UTC. Behavior 71 (`social-interest-radar-v2`, hourly `25 * * * *`)
has failed **15 consecutive runs since 2026-07-30T13:32 UTC** — ~12h dead. Every single one:

```
429 status code (no body)
```

Last success 2026-07-30T13:25 (run 807153). Confirms Gap 1 is not academic: switching the
org default from z-ai to Gemini did not add resilience, it just moved which vendor's quota
is the single point of failure. Gap 2's signature is visible too — one failed run per cron
tick, forever, because nothing parses the 429's reset.

Also note the 429 here has **no body**, so even the "park until the named reset" fix in
Gap 2 has nothing to parse on this provider. A per-`(org, provider)` cooldown needs a
default backoff for bodyless 429s, not just a `Retry-After` reader.

| `behaviors.model_config.model` (b71) | `run_sdk` → `client.behaviors.update` |

name: reference_behavior_prompt_bloat_and_zai_speed
description: "Why Behavior runs take 90s on z-ai/glm-5.2 — PREFILL dominates, because read_knowledge ships the same events TWICE (content + sources duplicate 1:1) and estimated_tokens under-reports the real prompt by ~7.5x"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 13f0fe8f-d0cb-4f1a-b19c-1621ef6e6b2b
  modified: 2026-07-31T01:43:27.765Z
---

Measured 2026-07-31 on prod behavior 71 (run 812212, 93s wall) after the switch to
`z-ai/glm-5.2` ([[project_behaviors_down_zai_quota]]).

## z.ai glm-5.2 is not slow — the prompt is huge

Controlled probes via `client.conversations.send({model:'z-ai/glm-5.2', wait:true})`:

| probe | result | derived |
|---|---|---|
| 2 chars out, tiny in | 7.8s | **fixed overhead ~7.8s** (worker spawn, MCP init, TTFT) |
| 9798 chars out, tiny in | 35.8s | **decode ~350 chars/s (~87 tok/s)** |
| 2 chars out, **506 KB in** | 33.6s | **prefill ~26s per 506 KB (~4.9K tok/s)** |

Run 812212 reconciles exactly: ~8s overhead + 2 calls carrying a ~537 KB prompt
(~27s prefill each = ~54s) + ~25s decoding the digest ≈ 93s. **Prefill is ~60% of the run**,
and the big context is paid TWICE — once on the call that emits `complete_window`, once on
the follow-up carrying its result.

## The prompt is bloated because read_knowledge DUPLICATES the events

`client.knowledge.read({behavior_id:71, since, until})` returned **325 KB**:

| block | size | note |
|---|---|---|
| `content` | **191 KB** | 200 items × 1541 B |
| `sources.recent_social` | **114 KB** | 200 items × 868 B |
| `sources.known_people` | 14 KB | 80 items |
| `sources.voice_profiles` | 4 KB | 4 items |

**`id_overlap` between `content` and `sources.recent_social` is 200/200 — the identical
events, serialized twice with different field sets.** A behavior whose source query merely
re-selects the window's own events pays for every event twice. `content` already carries
`id, platform, origin_type, payload_text, metadata, occurred_at`, so such a source is
redundant and can usually just be deleted.

`content` items also serialize dead fields per row: `payload_data:{}`,
`payload_template:null`, `attachments:[]`, `title:null`, `text_content`, `rating`, `score`,
`classifications`, `origin_parent_id`, `depth`.

## ⚠️ `estimated_tokens` under-reports by ~7.5x — do not size a prompt with it

The same response advertised `estimated_tokens: 10870` and `total_count_chars: 43479`,
while the actual serialized payload was 325 KB (~81K tokens). It counts `payload_text`
only, not the envelope. Size a Behavior prompt by
`JSON.stringify(knowledge).length`, never by `estimated_tokens`.

## Levers, measured

Cutting the 325 KB knowledge payload to ~95 KB (drop the redundant `recent_social`,
`left(payload_text,300)`, LIMIT 200 → 80) should take prefill from ~27s to ~5s per call
and the run from ~93s to roughly ~45s. Sources are version-owned: changing them needs
`behaviors.createVersion` **with `sources` passed explicitly** — calling it with only
`prompt` INHERITS the previous sources (observed: v242 came back `source_count: 3`).

Caveat on my own v242 prompt: asking for a specific per-item `why` plus `suggested_action`
increased decode vs the old boilerplate. Better output, slightly slower — the win is on the
prefill side, not decode.

## Reading the timing out of prod logs — two traps

1. **pino `responseTime` on `/lobu/api/proxy/…` is time-to-first-byte, NOT generation
   time.** `Stream delta` lines keep arriving after the request is logged "completed". A
   call logged `rt=11279ms` actually streamed for ~73s more.
2. **Tool-call arguments emit no delta logs.** While the model streams a `complete_window`
   argument, the log is silent — it looks like a stalled gap with no LLM activity. The
   giveaway is a later `sse-fanout ... skipped oversized "tool_use"` line.

Pods roll often (Flux image automation) — a pod that was 6m old was replaced minutes later
and its logs were gone. To profile a run, start `kubectl logs -f` into a file FIRST, then
trigger. See [[project_prod_flux_image_automation]].

Measured live on `:9186`, 2026-07-30.

Triggering Behavior `<id>` creates:

1. `runs` row with `run_type='behavior'`, `watcher_id` set, payload in
   **`approved_input`**, `action_input` **NULL**. Its id is what gets packed into
   the conversation id: `<agentId>_watcher_<behaviorId>_run_<THIS id>`.
2. One or more `runs` rows with `run_type='chat_message'`, payload in
   **`action_input`** (`{agentId, conversationId}`). One of these is the queue row
   `MessageConsumer` claims, so **its** id is `token.runId` and the `runId` in the
   transcript-snapshot POST body.

Concretely: conversation `owletto-default_watcher_1_run_109` checkpoints under
`runId=112`.

Consequences:

- **Never compare `parseBehaviorRunConversationId(conv).runId` against the
  request/token `runId`.** Different id spaces; the comparison is never true.
  This silently killed `stampBehaviorLastRun` — see
  [[project_behavior_listing_column]].
- `isRunOwnedByJwtScope` (transcript-routes) reads **only `action_input`**, so it
  authorizes against the chat_message row. A `run_type='behavior'` row can never
  satisfy it.
- A test fixture that derives the conversation id from the same id it mints the
  token with collapses the two spaces and will pass against broken code. Insert
  both rows. [[feedback_test_the_shape_production_throws]]

Related: [[reference_conversation_id_is_a_session_key]] — `conversation_id` is a
session key, and this is a second way its embedded ids are not what they look
like.

name: project_dual_executor_regression_2499
description: "Deploying #2499 broke every dual-executor Behavior (agent_id AND device_worker_id both set) — device-first precedence routes them to a device lane that often has no configured agent_kind executor; buremba b5/b71 died this way 2026-08-05 and I had dismissed exactly this risk as 'empirically empty'"

Found 2026-08-05 in org `buremba` while fixing Behaviors end-to-end.

## What happened

`#2499` (squash `317323f70`, merged 2026-08-05 13:08 +0100) makes a Behavior have exactly ONE
executor and resolves it **device-first**:

```
resolveBehaviorExecutor()  — tools/admin/manage_behaviors/executors.ts:57
  if (deviceWorkerId) return {kind:'device', …}   // ← wins
  if (agentId)        return {kind:'agent',  …}
  return null
```

Both lanes call it through `enqueueWatcherRunForRecord` (`watchers/automation.ts:247`) — the
scheduled lane via `createRun` (`automation.ts:848`) and the manual/event lane directly. **There is
no scheduled-vs-manual inconsistency**; I hypothesised one from the error messages and it was wrong.
The code check settled it in one grep — do that before asserting a lane split.

A row with BOTH `agent_id` and `device_worker_id` therefore silently stops using its agent the
moment #2499 rolls out. If the pinned device has no executor for the row's `agent_kind`, every run
hard-fails in <1s with:

    no local agent executor configured for agent_kind='opencode'

buremba `b5` (hourly-task-collaborator) and `b71` (social-interest-radar-v2) — the org's only two
active scheduled Behaviors — were both dual rows pinned to the Mac mini with `agent_kind='opencode'`,
which is not configured there. Fix was to drop the device pin:

    client.behaviors.update({ behavior_id:'71', device_worker_id:null, agent_kind:null })

b71 then completed in 48s (run 858655) and emitted a real "Social interest radar" digest.

## The dismissal that was wrong — and why

[[project_behavior_executors_pr_2499]] records that the claude reviewer flagged dual rows and that I
checked prod and concluded the risk was "empirically empty" because only 2 dual rows existed (b2
`crm`, b72 `personal-agent`) and neither was a chat responder. **b5 and b71 were dual rows too and I
missed them.** The population query was wrong or ran against the wrong scope; the conclusion
"therefore those 2 are the COMPLETE population" inherited that error and read as proof.

Generalises [[feedback_verify_dont_reason_from_construction]]: an enumeration is only evidence of
completeness if you can show the query that produced it covered the whole space. I wrote
"necessarily … so those 2 are the COMPLETE population" — a *deductive* argument standing in for a
count. The deduction was fine; the count it rested on was not.

## Do this before/after any executor-precedence deploy

Enumerate dual rows across ALL orgs, not one:

```sql
SELECT organization_id, id, agent_id, device_worker_id, agent_kind, status
FROM watchers
WHERE agent_id IS NOT NULL AND device_worker_id IS NOT NULL AND status = 'active';
```

Every hit is a Behavior whose executor is about to change. `query_sql` is org-scoped, so this needs
the CLI or a DB session — an org-scoped survey will under-count exactly the way mine did.
